title: MedlinePlus says newborn primitive reflexes fade by about 3 to 4 months
summary: MedlinePlus says the primitive reflexes it lists have disappeared, or started to disappear, by about 3 to 4 months.
body: MedlinePlus says that by 3 to 4 months, primitive reflexes have either already disappeared or are starting to disappear. The patterns it had listed for newborns include a fling of the arms, a turn toward a cheek, a finger grip, and supported steps. Disappeared, or starting to disappear, is the page's pair of words. That timing belongs to this encyclopedia's list. It does not say every infant loses each pattern on the same day, and it is not a diagnosis.
